route: What should happen to this pull request next, given what the body claims, what the changed paths show, and what the checks reported?

ready_for_manual_approval.description: every claim in the body is backed by something a reviewer could open and check, and nothing about the change demands a human reading the code

residual_risk.question: Supposing the evidence is complete, how much risk is still carried by merging this?

options.negligible: documentation, comments or an isolated change that cannot affect running behaviour
options.ordinary: a normal code change whose failure mode would be noticed and fixed
options.elevated: correct as far as anyone can tell, but a failure would be expensive or slow to notice

needs_release_note.question: Would someone outside this repository notice a difference after this is merged?

request_evidence.description: the body asserts an outcome that no artifact in the pull request lets a reviewer verify independently

missing.question: For the claim this pull request most needs to prove and currently does not, is {} the form of proof that would actually settle it?

options.command_output: the pasted output of a command that was actually run
options.ci_link: a link to a continuous integration run showing the result
options.log_excerpt: an excerpt of a log showing the behaviour before or after
options.commit_hash: a commit or revision identifier the claim applies to
options.screenshot: a picture of a rendered or visual result
options.reviewer_signoff: a named person confirming they checked it

severity.question: Does the missing proof block a decision, or is the claim incidental?
severity.stated: Does the body make the unproven claim central to why this should be merged?

options.blocking: the unproven claim is the reason this is being put forward
options.advisory: the unproven claim is a side remark the decision does not rest on

deep_review.description: a person has to read this code before it merges, whatever the evidence attached to it says

area.question: What is it about the changed paths that makes reading the code necessary?

options.auth_or_secrets: it touches who is allowed to do what, or handles credentials
options.data_or_migration: it changes stored data or the shape of it
options.deploy_or_infra: it changes how the system is built, released or run
options.shared_interface: it changes something many other parts depend on
options.external_effect: it causes something to happen outside this repository
options.complex_logic: the reasoning in the change is intricate enough that tests would not catch a subtle error

reviewer.question: Whose judgement is the one actually needed here?

options.security: someone who thinks about how this could be abused
options.data: someone who owns the correctness and shape of stored data
options.platform: someone who owns how the system is built and run
options.domain_owner: someone who knows what the feature is supposed to do

read_the_diff.question: Does the reviewer need to read the changed lines, rather than just the description?

hold.description: there is not enough here to send it down any other lane, or the signals contradict each other

reason.question: What is it that prevents a decision from being reached at all?

options.contradictory_evidence: two things in the pull request cannot both be true
options.insufficient_information: the body and paths do not say enough to judge
options.checks_unfinished: automated checks have not reported yet
options.scope_undefined: what this change is supposed to accomplish was never stated
